name: Sohrab Ahmari

lean.basis: Neoconservative writer (Wall Street Journal opinion pages, Commentary) who criticized Trump, Putin and Le Pen as part of a global illiberal trend.

Turned to post-liberal "common-good" conservatism ("Against David French-ism", 2019), backed Trump and Orbán, and served as an adviser to Vice President JD Vance; combines social conservatism with pro-worker economics.

current_role: US editor of UnHerd; founding editor of Compact; adviser to Vice President JD Vance
summary: Sohrab Ahmari (born 1985 in Tehran) is an Iranian-American writer and editor, formerly op-ed editor of the New York Post. A convert to Catholicism, he broke with "David French-ism" in 2019 and became a leading post-liberal voice; in 2022 he co-founded the magazine Compact. Wikipedia describes him as an adviser to Vice President Vance in Trump's second term; in June 2026 he flew with Vance to Switzerland for talks with Iran without a security clearance.

timeline.role: Co-founder and founding editor (with Matthew Schmitz and Edwin Aponte)

connections.name: JD Vance
connections.description: Wikipedia describes Ahmari as an adviser to Vice President Vance in Trump's second term; in June 2026 he flew with Vance on Air Force Two to Switzerland for talks with Iran, without a security clearance.

connections.name: Yoram Hazony
connections.description: Ahmari spoke at Hazony's NatCon in 2021.

connections.name: George Soros
connections.description: Vanity Fair reported that Compact received extensive funding from the Soros family's Open Society Foundations; contested, since Salon earlier said Peter Thiel was behind it.

connections.name: Tucker Carlson
connections.description: After Carlson's September 2024 interview with Darryl Cooper, who cast Churchill as WWII's "chief villain", Ahmari called Cooper's claims "the same old Hitler apologetic" and warned that such views were moving from the fringe to the mainstream.

sources.title: Tucker Carlson's WWII interview fractures conservatives — The Week
World War II and the rise of anti-history — The Free Press

connections.name: R. R. Reno
connections.description: Ahmari is a First Things columnist; his 2019 essay "Against David French-ism" ran in Reno's magazine.

connections.name: Patrick Deneen
connections.description: Leading figures of the "post-liberal" right, routinely reviewed and named together; Deneen's Regime Change and Ahmari's Tyranny, Inc. (both 2023) were read as companion books.

sources.title: On Sohrab Ahmari's Tyranny, Inc. and Patrick J. Deneen's Regime Change — LA Review of Books

source_conflicts.details: Salon reported that Peter Thiel was behind Compact; a later Vanity Fair report said it received extensive funding from the Soros family's Open Society Foundations, contradicting Salon.
